title: On one GOES flux scale, HMI magnetic flux reduces the Cycle 25 M-flare excess over Cycle 24 from 1.55 to 1.15-1.21, and the remaining excess is in multi-region complexes (NOAA and SDO data 2010-2026)
abstract: Question: on one GOES X-ray flux scale, which description of solar activity gives the same M-flare rate in different solar cycles, and where is the remaining Cycle 25 excess? Method: we used the NOAA/SWPC flare list on the true (science) flux scale from a prior campaign publication, 45,202 SWPC Solar Region Summary region-days (1998-2026) and 42,115 SDO/HMI SHARP records (2010-05 to 2026-10). We modelled the daily full-disk flare count as the sum of the rates of the regions on the disk, with one factor per cycle, and we predicted each cycle from fits to the other cycles. Intervals come from a 27-day block bootstrap. Results: at matched SRS area, Hale class, McIntosh class, spot count and neighbour regions, Cycle 25 regions give 1.54 (95% CI 1.31-1.83) times more M1+ flares than Cycle 24 regions, so region composition explains none of the per-sunspot excess. On the same 2010-2026 days, the Cycle 25/Cycle 24 ratio is 1.55 (1.29-1.90) with SRS regions and 1.15 (0.91-1.54) with the HMI unsigned flux of each active-region patch (1.21, 1.08-1.47, with flux, R and TOTUSJH); the paired reduction is 1.28 (1.10-1.47). For M5+ and X1+ flares the HMI ratio is 0.98 and 0.89. Patches with one SRS region flare at the same rate per unit flux in both cycles (0.99, 0.69-1.38); patches with two or more regions flare 1.72 (1.23-2.57) times more in Cycle 25, and they give 61% of the Cycle 25 M flares (Cycle 24: 29%). No full-disk index predicts all three cycles: held-out observed/predicted ratios are 0.65/0.90/1.58 with sunspot number and 0.73/1.21/1.15 with F10.7. On one scale, M flares per delta region are 3.6, 3.5 and 3.8 in Cycles 23-25; the operational scale makes Cycle 25 delta regions seem 1.5 times more productive. Limitations: HMI covers only Cycles 24-25, Cycle 25 is incomplete, the multi-region split depends on HARP and NOAA numbering, and the variant bootstraps have only 20 replicates.

display.caption: Cycle 25/Cycle 24 (blue) and Cycle 23/Cycle 24 (green, panel a) M1+ rate ratios at matched normalization on the true GOES flux scale, with 95% block-bootstrap intervals. Crosses: operational scale. Panel b uses the same 2010-2026 days for all models; green points use HMI SHARP parameters.

a. Share of SRS spot area and of M1+ flares in HMI patches (HARPs) that contain two or more SRS regions. b. Cycle 25/Cycle 24 M1+ rate per HARP-day at matched HMI flux or SRS area, for single-region (blue) and multi-region (orange) HARPs, on the true and the operational scale.

citations.reason: We use its true-scale flare peaks and NCEI detection counts. We confirm its F10.7 and sunspot results on one scale and test its proposed explanation of the per-sunspot excess with HMI flux.
